title: Why You Prefer Things You Have Seen Before
hook: Why do you always pick the same brand of coffee?

narration.text: Your brain is wired to prefer things you have encountered many times before.
This is called the mere exposure effect, a powerful psychological phenomenon.
Repeated exposure makes something feel more familiar and therefore safer.
We tend to like things that pose less of an unknown threat.
This effect shapes your preferences, from music to people you meet.
It is why advertisers repeat slogans or show you the same product many times.
It builds trust and positive feelings over time.
Have you noticed yourself picking familiar options in your daily life?

description: Ever wonder why you gravitate towards the same brands, songs, or even people? It is all down to the mere exposure effect. Discover how familiarity shapes your preferences and influences your daily choices.
topic: Why you tend to prefer things you have seen before, explaining the mere exposure effect.
